practical.daily_checks: Wind is the real disruptor, not cold. Anything over 15 m/s makes waterfall stops miserable and can tear a car door off its hinges — always hold doors when opening.
practical.fuel_cards: Icelandic self-service pumps need a 4-digit PIN on a foreign chip card. Set this up before you fly. Choose a fixed amount rather than 'fill up' to avoid a large pre-authorisation hold.

Highland F-road, shut by late September
Usually not open until mid-November. Katla is the alternative

practical.volcanic_status: The Reykjanes peninsula has erupted repeatedly since 2023–24 near Sundhnúkur/Grindavík. Grindavík town remains largely restricted; the Blue Lagoon is open as of mid-2026. Conditions change fast — check almannavarnir.is and vedur.is on the day.
practical.northern_lights: Genuinely possible from Day 2 onward. Check the aurora forecast on vedur.is each evening (combined cloud cover + Kp). Get clear of town lights. Best bases: Hvolsvöllur, Hof, Grundarfjörður.
practical.coffee_reality: Outside Reykjavík and the Golden Circle, cafés are sparse and many rural ones cut hours in October. Reliable sit-down stops: Geysir, Skógafoss, Vík, Arnarstapi, Hraunfossar. Everywhere else it's an N1 petrol station — which is fine, but not a lingering experience.
practical.fuel_stops: Fill up at Vík and at Kirkjubæjarklaustur or Höfn. Do not assume you'll find a station further east.
